fact: In 2005, my galleries hosted 21 exhibitions. The flagship exhibition was 'Hatched: National Graduate Show 2005' (showcasing 60 emerging artists). Other major exhibitions that year were Shiro Takatani's media installations (as part of the Japan-Australia exchange RAPT! project), Richard Giblett's work in the 'New Dystopias' group show, and photographer Tony Nathan's solo exhibition 'Proof of Light' (October 20 – November 13, 2005).

In 2005, PICA's CEO and Director was Sarah Miller. Hannah Mathews served as a key curator on my team (starting her curatorial tenure at PICA from 2005 to 2008), shaping the year's experimental visual arts program alongside guest curators.

Artists who exhibited in 2005 include photographer Tony Nathan (solo exhibition 'Proof of Light'), Shiro Takatani (media arts), Richard Giblett (New Dystopias), and Hatched graduates Tom Halliday, Natalie Preiato, Shannon Lyons, Keumhee Oh, Stephanie Hicks, Alex James, Paul Wotherspoon, Joanne Gerke, Rebecca Jones, and Ryan Nazzari.

My history features key directors: Noel Sheridan (founding director, 1989-1993) who set my experimental and multidisciplinary tone; Sarah Miller (1993-2006) who expanded national presence; Amy Barrett-Lennard (2006-2022) who focused on residency commissions; and Hannah Mathews (2022-Present) who Curates research-driven collaborations. Sarah Wall is currently the Curator.

In 2005, I hosted 13 performance works. My long history of performance includes Joan Jonas' mirror performance 'Mirror Piece I & II' (restaged in 2024 for Bunuru season/Perth Festival), Cassils' performance 'Becoming an Image' in their ALCHEMIC show, Amrita Hepi's 'Monumental' choreographic video work, Laure Prouvost (2025), and Francesca Lasica's 'WHEN I AM NOT THERE' season.

PICA Bar & Cafe operates on my front ground-floor verandah, serving as a popular social hub in the Perth Cultural Centre where artists, curators, and visitors gather for drinks, coffee, and discussions.

I was designed in 1896 in the Federation Free Classical style by architect George Temple Poole, featuring red face-brick, stucco details, a central double-height hall, and a signature landmark clock tower on James Street.

Architects Donaldson and Warn designed my major refurbishment in 1991, converting the former segregated boys' school layout into galleries and a performance space, officially opening as PICA on November 8, 1991.

Opened in 1897 as the Perth Boys' and Girls' School (part of the Perth Central School complex). It was segregated, with boys on the ground floor and girls on the first floor. From 1959 to 1988, I was a branch of Perth Technical College (TAFE) before becoming PICA in 1989.

My signature visual art programs include 'Hatched: National Graduate Show' (annual flagship since 1992 showcasing visual arts graduates) and the Judy Wheeler Commission (annual site-specific visual arts commission activating my front lobby and glass facade).
From April 18 to June 14, 2026, my galleries hosted 'Revealed: New and Emerging WA Aboriginal Artists' (showcasing new WA Aboriginal artists) and Dellas Bennell's 'Where Waters Meet' in my PICA Hub.

In July 2026, I hosted the contemporary dance show 'Restore' by STRUT Dance (July 15-18, 2026) accompanied by post-show artist talks featuring Ainslie Allen, Annika Moses, Brooke Stamp, and Daniel Jenatsch. I also hosted 'On Labour: Four Live Works' (July 2-4, 2026) featuring live works by Grace Connors, Barbara Hostalek, Sukhjit Kaur Khalsa, and Sarah Rodigari.

In mid-2026, my studio spaces hosted numerous resident artists, including Benjamin Quirk (Quick Response, July 13-26), Kumo-bako/Ken Meyer (Quick Response, June 15 - July 5), Lauren Jane Salt (Quick Response, June 15 - July 5), Maraya Takoniatis (Quick Response, June 1-14), Mohammed 'Ayo Busari' with blue joy theatre company (May 25 - June 14), Naoko Uemoto for the BREEZE Perth-Makassar International Exchange Residency (May 11 - June 7), Germaine Chan (May 4-24), Liv McIntyre (May 4-31), and Grace Connors for Bluebird23 (May 2 - June 21).

My 2026 public program featured diverse events, including the Reconciliation Week: Revealed In Conversation panel (May 30, 2026), the First Nations Curating Panel (June 11, 2026) with curators Glenn Iseger-Pilkington and Ilona McGuire, a film screening of 'Dungku Asang' (May 2, 2026), the Open Studios: Djeran showcase (April 29, 2026), and hand block printing workshops led by Nagula Jarndu (April 18, 2026).
